content:
The test image shows a tomato stem split longitudinally, revealing:
- Brown/tan internal vascular and pith discoloration with streaking
- External whitish lesion with concentric ring-like banding on the stem
- Location at or near the soil line (black plastic mulch visible)
- Plant has collapsed with wilted/dead leaves

Top candidates: **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers** (concentric rings on stem near soil line, cracked/dry vascular tissue), **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt** (brown pith discoloration), **Verticillium_Wilt** (vascular browning in cut stem).

The concentric ring pattern on the exterior and internal browning near soil line most strongly suggests Alternaria. Let me confirm with one reference image.

Comparing test vs reference:

**Test image**: Stem dissected lengthwise showing internal brown vascular/pith streaking, exterior has whitish-tan lesion with concentric ring banding, at soil line, plant collapsed.

**Reference (Alternaria)**: Dark brown-black canker girdling stem at soil line — quite dark and collapsed.

The test image shows a lighter lesion with more visible concentric ring banding and internal cracked/dry brown vascular streaking. This matches the Alternaria description: "large, irregularly shaped, dark-brown to almost black cankers with **light and dark concentric rings**" and "vascular and pith tissue... develop brown streaks and become **cracked and dry**." The dissected stem showing internal browning near the soil line fits well.

Southern_Bacterial_Wilt could also fit (brown pith discoloration), but there's no visible bacterial ooze. Verticillium_Wilt shows V-shaped leaf lesions rather than stem cankers as the primary sign.

The concentric ring pattern on the exterior + internal vascular browning + soil line location aligns best with Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers.
